source.section: PDF page 18, Schedule S Part B Line 20 (Bailey: TSERS retiree with five or more years of creditable service as of August 12, 1989); PDF page 14, Lines 11, 14, 15

worked: Federal AGI = NC Teachers' and State Employees' Retirement System pension 40,000.00 + interest 750.00 = 40,750.00. Projection: Bailey is not_modelled, so the pension is taxed (no Line 20 deduction). Federal taxable income = 40,750.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 23,000.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). D-400 Line 6 federal AGI 40,750.00. Line 7 additions (Schedule S Part A) 0.00. Line 8 = Line 6 + Line 7 = 40,750.00. Line 9 deductions (Schedule S Part B) 0.00. Line 10 child deduction 0.00 (no qualifying children). Line 11 NC standard deduction (single) 12,750.00. Line 12a = Lines 9 + 10 + 11 = 12,750.00; Line 12b = Line 8 - Line 12a = 28,000.00. Line 14 NC taxable income (full-year resident) = 28,000.00. Line 15 tax = 28,000.00 x 0.0425 = 1,190.00. Line 16 credits 0.00; Line 17 income tax = 1,190.00. The booklet itself would deduct 40,000.00 on Schedule S Line 20: Line 12b = 40,750.00 - 40,000.00 - 12,750.00 = -12,000.00, tax 0.00; the projection overstates tax by 1,190.00 (4.25% of the 28,000.00 of taxable income it keeps).
accepted_approximations: The Bailey exclusion (Schedule S Line 20) is not applied (not_modelled): qualifying NC state, NC local and US government civilian retirement benefits (and the state's 401(k) and 457 plans) are taxed. Military retired pay is not taxed: it is deducted under Line 21 (see the maintainer assumption).
